can_evaluate: 1. Grep for the tracker model class and confirm it has fields: total_attempts, failure_count, degraded_count, and a timestamped history collection.
2. Confirm a standalone classification function/method exists that maps a single route() outcome to exactly one of {acceptable, degraded, invalid}; verify exhaustiveness by reading the mapping logic.

3. Confirm the rolling-rate computation accepts a window_days parameter with default=7; verify the return value is per-tick-type and covers boundary conditions (empty history, window shorter than data).
4. Read simulate_day_bridged: confirm there is a branch that compares rolling rate to threshold and, when exceeded, skips the LLM call and takes the deterministic path.
5. Confirm AppraisalAuditLog (or an attached field) records auto_fallback_triggered=True and a reason string when fallback fires; verify a test asserts this field is populated.
6. Confirm recovery logic: when window slides past degraded entries the flag clears; verify a test demonstrates LLM path is retried after a sufficient number of clean days.
7. Confirm simulate_day_bridged signature has the tracker as an optional parameter (default None); confirm a test calls it without the parameter and verifies identical behavior to current code.
8. Run pytest back/tests/ with no test file modifications and confirm zero failures.
9. Confirm new test functions exist covering: outcome classification, rolling rate computation, threshold-triggered fallback, and window-based recovery (four distinct test areas).
